=== THE ROOT CAUSE, recorded here too because it is what keeps doing this ===

Not a finding against #46. scripts/lwb_lanes.py's commit_files() runs `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r --root <sha>`, which prints NOTHING for a merge commit, so commit_files(<any merge>) is []; _is_record_only_commit returns False on an empty list (deliberately, against the empty-commit trap). Every merge is therefore classified as a content change and moves the reviewable head. I measured this exactly on PR #51, where merge 07f82d1 -- whose entire first-parent payload is two reviews/51/ files, and whose own message says "bring in both independent review records" -- moved the reviewable head onto itself and staled both records it had just brought in. The act of merging a review record destroys it. That is HANDOFF item 5's own pattern: diff-tree printing no lines for a merge means "no combined diff", not "changed nothing". Suggested fix, offered and untested: classify a multi-parent commit by its first-parent diff, keeping the empty-commit guard as an explicit separate case.
